newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate down on mild U.S. inflation.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate down on mild U.S. inflation.

text.p: Mexican overnight Cetes rates were down 35 basis points at 23.70 percent in early trade on Tuesday in response to a strong peso and sliding U.S. long bond yields following the release of mild U.S. consumer price data, traders said.
"We expected overnight rates to rise under pressure from yesterday's secondary auctions when assignment rates soared, jacked up by big players that have all the cash," a money market analyst said.
Banco de Mexico drained 9.490 billion pesos on Monday by assigning secondary auctions at rates of 26.40-28.70 percent.
Benchmark 48-hour peso contracts were 3.1 centavos stronger in early dealings at 7.8850/7.8890 per dollar.
The U.S. 30-year Treasury bond was meanwhile up 31/32 to yield 7.09 percent in response to what traders said were U.S. consumer prices that "came in lower than expected."
Overnight rates on bank paper had meanwhile fallen 90 basis points to 25.60 percent.

Nonetheless, traders said secondary rates could come under pressure during the session from forecast increases in primary rates at Banco de Mexico's weekly auction of government securities, to be held later in the day.
"Market speculation is paving the way for an automatic increase in primary rates, which at the same time is exerting pressure on secondary rates," a money market analyst said.
Other analysts said primary rates could gain in order to tighten monetary policy because the monetary base in Mexico had increased above levels forecast by the central bank.
In a report by the Interacciones brokerage, chief economist Alonso Cervera wrote that the causes for the increase in the monetary base were not clear and may require explanation.

"If the monetray base does not adjust in a sustained way to the levels expected by the central bank, we would expect the adoption of a more restrictive monetary policy or an explanation why the official projections have temporarily not been met," Cervera wrote.
Liquidity of 4.518 billion pesos was slated to return to the system on Tuesday from prior central bank participation.
